Section 1 · World artificial surf reefs

Artificial surf reefs around the world — what was built, what it cost, how it ended

A survey of the 13 artificial surf reefs we could document as actually built, 1997–2025, in 6 countries: what each one was meant to do, what was really built, what it cost, who paid, and how it turned out. It is written for municipal decision-makers and surfers weighing a reef for the Israeli coast. Open any reef for the big picture first — an at-a-glance strip and the outcome — then dig into the sections you care about. Every fact carries a numbered source marker [R#]: tap or hover it to see the source without losing your place. Compiled 2026-09-25.

Showing 13 of 13 reefs

Each reef is drawn in plan view — sea at the top, beach at the bottom — at one common scale, so the drawings can be compared directly. The outlines are documented schematics built from published dimensions, design drawings and photos, not surveys: every number below carries its source, or says that it is derived from our own drawing. Open How we drew this under any drawing for the full derivation, the images relied on, the comparison with Gemini's earlier attempt, and open issues. A football pitch is taken as 105 × 68 m (FIFA recommendation) = 7,140 m².

Lior's reference graphic traces outlines over real aerial photos. We did not have geo-referenced aerial imagery for all 13 reefs (and this pass added no new images), so we draw the outlines on a plain sea/beach background instead.

3 · Coordinate conventions and notes

Coordinates
metres; origin = shoreline point nearest the reef centroid; x = alongshore (positive toward north -- the Narrowneck isthmus trends roughly N-S per general regional geography, no source gives an exact shoreline azimuth); y = offshore (positive seaward); shoreline approximated as the line y=0.
Shape
Dual-arm split-V / chevron: two separate wishbone-shaped reef units ('north arm' and 'south arm' in this report's own labelling) set side by side alongshore, joined by a narrow central channel across which a small submerged weir (two containers) was added in 2004. Confirmed by text and four plan-view figures in the primary monitoring paper (Jackson et al. 2012, []). This is NOT an inshore/offshore concentric-lobe arrangement (see gemini_comparison).
Polygon
polygons_m[0] = north arm (x>0), polygons_m[1] = south arm (x<0, mirror image of the north arm in x). Both closed and non-self-intersecting (checked with shapely: is_valid=True, is_simple=True for both). No solid polygon is given for the central channel/waist (x approx -50 to 50) since it is open water crossed only by a small 2-container weir added in 2004, not a filled structure -- see md derivation/'Polygon construction'.
Orientation
Two arms (north/south) run alongshore either side of a central channel/weir, matching the card's pre-existing 'split V shape... paddling channel between the arms' language [][]. The reef is understood to face the Gold Coast's predominant E-ESE swell (general regional geography, open east-facing coast), consistent with (though not independently confirmed to the same precision as) Gemini's claimed 090-120 deg incident swell direction -- no source found by either this report or Gemini states a precise degree figure. Alongshore axis 'north' is this report's own convention, not a sourced compass bearing.
Other published size
A second source [] gives a conflicting 450 m (long) x 250 m (wide) for this same reef; not reconciled with the 600x350 [] figure used for this file's bounding box and polygon scaffold. Both are retained per the project reference rule.
Area
Net area of the two schematic arm polygons above (shoelace formula: 57,475 m^2 each), NOT a published or surveyed figure -- it is a geometric consequence of this report's own illustrative vertex placement (see md 'Polygon construction'). Gross bounding-box area (600x350) = 210,000 m^2. Not directly comparable to Gemini's gross (75,000) or net (42,650) figures since Gemini's underlying shape (inshore/offshore lobes) differs from the alongshore-split shape used here.
Crest depth datum
below low tide waterline (approx. LAT), as stated in sources -- design/2012 value
Crest depth over time
Crest depth is time-varying and this single value should not be used without noting its date: as designed/1999 and as of the 2012 primary-source survey, crest was 'about 1-1.5m below low tide' [ p.13, also ][]; by 2017, before the 2018 renewal, it had settled to 2.5-2.6 m below low tide []; the 2018 renewal added 84 containers to raise the crest again but no source gives a specific post-renewal number.
Distance measured from
shoreline -- treated as the reef's shoreward/inner edge; no source specifies exactly which point 'X m offshore' is measured to
Materials
Sand-filled non-woven geotextile containers ('mega sandbags'), approx. 450 placed by 1999-2006 (arithmetic per [] p.3/Fig.4: ~408 from the original 1999-2000 construction + top-up, plus 42 in three later maintenance campaigns 2002-2006 [Fig.4 table: 10+15+17=42] = 450 total; separately and independently gives a rounded 'more than 400' for the original build, consistent with ~408 but not an exact match to a card-invented '400') + 84 more added June 2018 [][]; each container approx. 20 m long, 3.0-4.8 m diameter [/ exact figure; corrected this pass from an earlier '3-4.5 m' rounding].
Confidence
medium

5 · Open issues

  • No plan-view figure with a legible printed scale bar was found for this reef in any source consulted (primary paper, ICM webpage, or the card's image list); the polygon vertices in this file are a documented schematic, not a survey-grade digitization.
  • The card's own pre-existing footprint disagreement (350x600m [] vs. 450x250m []) remains unreconciled; no third, tie-breaking source was found.
  • This report assumes north/south mirror symmetry between the two arms for the schematic polygon; Jackson et al. 2012 Fig. 4 suggests the two arms may not be perfectly identical, but source resolution does not support characterizing the actual asymmetry.
  • The exact shoreline azimuth at Narrowneck (to convert 'alongshore = positive north' into a true compass bearing) was not found in any source consulted; the isthmus's roughly N-S trend is inferred from general regional geography, not a stated figure.
  • Crest depth is genuinely time-varying (~1.0-1.5m as designed/2012 -> ~2.5-2.6m by 2017 settled -> an unstated, presumably shallower figure after the 2018 renewal); any single crest-depth number used elsewhere for this reef should specify which date/state it refers to.
  • The central channel's width (~100m, used to space the two arms in the schematic polygon) is this report's own unsourced assumption, not a published figure.
  • (Added 2026-09-25 verification pass) 's exact text is an unordered pair '350 x 600 m' with no stated axis; this file's 600=alongshore/350=cross-shore assignment (used in bbox_m and the polygon construction) is this report's own inference, not sourced.

3 · Coordinate conventions and notes

Coordinates
metres; origin = shoreline point nearest the reef centroid (exact shoreline position unknown - Xala's precise coordinates are undisclosed); x = alongshore (positive direction arbitrary/unconfirmed - no source states compass orientation of the reef or shoreline), y = offshore (positive seaward); shoreline approximated as the line y=0
Shape
No source describes or shows the reef's planform. This polygon is a symmetric footprint ENVELOPE only (not a confirmed chevron/V/delta shape) sized by open analogy to the same designer's only other published reef (Palm Beach Reef). It is not a measurement of Xala itself.
Orientation
Completely unconfirmed. No source states which way the reef's arms/apex point, the angle of the structure to the shore, or which compass direction is 'alongshore-positive'. Outcome text for Xala (card `outcome` field) explicitly states no independent surf report exists, so we do not even know whether Xala breaks right, left, or both (Palm Beach, the analogy source, breaks predominantly right with a shorter left in bigger swell, per - but that is Palm Beach's documented behaviour, not Xala's).
Area
Shoelace area of the polygon above: 11,200 m² (stored value 11,200 m²).
Crest depth datum
below MSL (analogy value; not stated for Xala) Design-analogy estimate only; no Xala-specific source gives a crest depth. Uncertainty large, plausibly anywhere between the surf-zone-minimum needed to be surfable at low tide (~0.5 m) and ~2.5 m.

shoreline (analogy value; not stated for Xala) Design-analogy estimate only; no Xala-specific source gives an offshore distance.

4 · Gemini comparison (Gemini's values are unverified; shown only to explain differences)

Where we agree

  • Materials/construction method (3,000 truckloads of quarried rock, no geotextile) - directly sourced and matches our own card [][].
  • Designer identity and Palm Beach Reef pedigree - matches our card [][].
  • Directionally, Gemini's numbers are in the same order of magnitude as ours, which is itself telling (see disagree notes below) - both land close to Palm Beach Reef's real 160x80m/1.5m/270m dimensions.
QuantityGeminiOursWhy ours

Gemini's Key Technical Specifications section presents '~140 x 75 m' with a tilde but with zero citation tying it to any of the 4 listed references, none of which is an engineering drawing or contains a number close to 140 or 75. The number cannot be derived from Gemini's own source list. Our own value (160m) is at least traceable to a real, cited, quoted figure - Palm Beach Reef's published dimension - and is labeled throughout as an unverified analogy, not a Xala fact.

This phrase looks like it was generalized from Palm Beach Reef's documented behavior (a right-hander plus a shorter left in bigger swell) or from generic surf-reef design language, not from anything published about Xala.

5 · Open issues

  • No source found by either this project's exhaustive card/dossier sweep (2026-09-24) or this footprint task's re-check (2026-09-25) discloses any Xala-specific length, width, area, crest depth, or offshore distance.
  • No aerial photo, plan-view figure, engineering drawing, permit filing, or CAD/scale asset for Xala exists in this project's media indexes, in Gemini's media indexes, or in Gemini's reef_footprints.json (confirmed by direct grep - the Gemini slug 'xala-reef-mexico' has no entry in the structures array at all).
  • The only two verified images of Xala (both already in the card's `images` list) are close-range, water-level surf action photos with no shoreline, scale reference, or plan view visible - confirmed by direct visual inspection this task.
  • This entire footprint record is therefore a labeled DESIGN-ANALOGY PLACEHOLDER (to the designer's only other published reef, Palm Beach), not a Xala measurement or a figure-based estimate. It should be replaced the moment a real design paper, permit drawing, or aerial photo of Xala's reef becomes available.
  • Exact reef coordinates and shoreline orientation are undisclosed, so the coordinate frame's alongshore-positive direction is arbitrary and cannot be tied to a compass heading.
  • Whether Xala's reef is symmetric, single-armed, or a chevron/V like Palm Beach is completely unconfirmed; the polygon supplied here is a symmetric envelope specifically to avoid asserting an unconfirmed asymmetric/chevron shape.

3 · Coordinate conventions and notes

Coordinates
metres; origin = shoreline point directly onshore of the reef's photo-measured centroid; x = alongshore (positive toward east, i.e. toward Bournemouth Pier direction / away from Boscombe Pier, matching the card's '~240 m east of the pier' framing); y = offshore (positive seaward); shoreline approximated as the line y=0.
Shape
A single elongated, asymmetric angled bank/ramp ("the reef doesn't create waves...it acts as a ramp", ) built from parallel geotextile tubes -- not a multi-armed chevron, V, or triangular delta. The already-verified aerial photo (raisedwaterresearch.com 'Boscombe-Arial') shows one coherent dark parallelogram-shaped patch with internal parallel stripes (individual container tubes), not two separate arms meeting at an apex.
Orientation
Long axis trends WSW-ENE: the deeper/offshore end sits to the WSW (photo-measured bearing of the offshore-pointing axis is roughly 245-250 deg), the shallower/nearshore end to the ENE. This is broadly consistent with the design intent stated in -- 'It's angled to catch the mean wave direction' for the dominant SSW-SW Channel swell (approx. 200-230 deg per the master comparative table Gemini also uses) -- though our photo-derived bearing (~247 deg) sits a little west of that swell window's centre; no source gives an exact design bearing figure, so this is a medium/low-confidence photo estimate, not a stated design number. The reef also produces an asymmetric wave (long right / short left, /), consistent with an asymmetric plan shape, but the photo resolution was not sufficient to confirm a sharper 'peeling corner' at one end versus a simple tapered rectangle.
Plan box note
Axis-aligned envelope in the shore-parallel/shore-normal frame. This is much bigger than the structure's own along-ramp footprint (187.5 m x 58 m) because the ramp's long axis is tilted roughly 24 deg off the shore-normal (offshore) direction -- see derivation. Do not read 'length_alongshore' here as the reef's own long dimension.
Area
Shoelace area of the polygon above: 10,862 m² (stored value 10,862 m²).
Crest depth datum
metres ABOVE Lowest Astronomical Tide / spring low water datum (positive = emergent, i.e. the reef's designed crest sits above this level after sand settlement, not below it). Sign convention clarified 2026-09-25 (was stored as -0.5 with an inverted-sign explanation, which was confusing to compare against Gemini's differently-signed convention); the underlying fact is unchanged.
Distance measured from
seawall base ('s exact figure and phrasing); cross-checked against (225 m from the beach) and (210 m from the shoreline) corrected 2026-09-25: previously mis-cited as ref , but 's own text states 210 m, not 220 m; is the source that literally states "220m from the base of the seawall".
Materials
~55 large sand-filled geotextile containers ('geobags'), each reported as approx. 2-3 m high x 60 m long (); one later source instead describes '56 sandbags between 50 and 70 metres long' built 'in two layers', with 'the biggest sandbags 2.5m high and 5m wide' () -- bag-count/size figures conflict across sources and are treated as approximate, not reconciled here.
Confidence
medium

5 · Open issues

  • No single authoritative engineering plan-view drawing or bathymetric survey of Boscombe Surf Reef could be located online (search engines used for this pass returned CAPTCHA walls; only already-cited pages and their linked images/figures were consulted, per task rules). The 'Diagram showing layout of the geotextile bags' on Wikipedia is a simplified cartoon, not a scaled drawing.
  • The reef's overall plan-view length (this file's 187.5 m) is a photo-based estimate, not a text-sourced figure; treat it as medium-low confidence pending a real design drawing or survey.
  • Container/bag count and size are inconsistent across sources: says '55 containers, 2-3 m high, 60 m long, ~1,000 t total'; says '56 sandbags, 50-70 m long, in two layers, biggest bags 2.5 m high x 5 m wide'. Neither this file nor the card resolves the discrepancy.
  • Area is reported two ways in real sources: 'one hectare / 2.5 acres' (, -- used here) vs. 'the area of a football pitch' (, which at a standard pitch size, ~7,140 m2, is notably smaller). Not reconciled; the hectare figure was preferred because two independent sources agree on it and it is corroborated by our own photo measurement.
  • The photo-derived long-axis bearing (~245-250 deg) assumes the aerial photo is close to north-up, inferred only from the pier's visible orientation and general knowledge of the Bournemouth coastline, not from an EXIF heading or map overlay -- treat the bearing as approximate.
  • Individual-image measurement was done on a single relatively low-resolution, refraction-blurred aerial photo; a second/higher-resolution aerial or satellite image (e.g. Google Maps/Earth imagery of the same site) would meaningfully tighten these estimates but was not pursued here to stay within the task's 'no new photo searches' rule (Google Maps was only listed as a card image lead, not fetched as a new search).

It is broadly consistent with the final 62,800 t tonnage at a plausible placed-rock bulk density (~1.6-1.9 t/m3 including voids, vs ~2.6-2.7 t/m3 for solid granite), which would imply ~33,000-39,000 m3 — no contradiction, but not independently confirmed.

The figure is still not used for precise scaled-vertex tracing (out of caution, given this residual ~10% offset and the schematic nature of the annotations), but the polygon's 165x110 m envelope comes directly from the sourced text quotes, not from pixel tracing, so this correction does not change any reported dimension — only the methodology note.

3 · Coordinate conventions and notes

Coordinates
metres; origin = shoreline point nearest the reef centroid (Middleton Beach, near the 'Surfer's Beach' car park); x = alongshore (positive toward north — assumed from the apparent north-up orientation of the Bluecoast/ASR design figure [], which shows dunes/land to the west and open water to the east, consistent with Middleton Beach's real north-south shoreline trend; no explicit north arrow is printed on the figure, so this is an inference, see open_issues); y = offshore (positive seaward); shoreline approximated as the line y=0
Shape
crescent
Orientation
The Bluecoast/ASR 'Final Reef Design' table (reproduced as a figure on , filename design.jpg) specifies 'Crest orientation: Curved, 270°N-305°N... Maximises breaking and creates waves that peel evenly along the reef.' This is the bearing of the reef's own curved crest/wave-break line (a ~35 degree arc), not a stated swell-approach azimuth — no source we found gives a numeric swell-approach bearing (contrary to Gemini's invented '160-190 deg SSE-S', see gemini_comparison). The design table also specifies 'Surfing direction: Left-hander' and a 'Take-off area' at the more offshore, wider end of the reef (per the same figure), with the wave peeling toward the narrower, more shoreward end, matching 's text 'the design provides surfing rides of up to 100m'. Our polygon therefore tapers to a point at its shoreward/updrift-adjacent end and bulges to its maximum ~110 m cross-shore width at the offshore 'take-off' end, per this figure — but the figure's own two dimension-arrow annotations (110 m and 140 m) do not share a consistent pixel scale (see derivation row 8), so this reading is topological/qualitative only, not a scaled tracing.
Area
Shoelace area of the polygon above: 9,720 m² (stored value 9,720 m²).
Crest depth datum
below AHD (Australian Height Datum, ≈ mean sea level); ≈0.74 m below mean low water, ≈1.34 m below mean high water
Distance measured from
shoreline / landward toe of the reef, per the Bluecoast/ASR concept-design table ('Cross-shore position: 140m from landward toe') reproduced on the City of Albany project page; our polygon's near (shoreward) tips sit at y=140-145 and its centroid sits at y≈189
Materials
Submerged rock-berm surf reef; ~62,800 t of layered granite in three graded layers — belly (D50 0.16 m, 12,400 t, 18%), core (D50 0.49 m, 23,600 t, 36%), Class 1 armour (D50 0.94 m, 26,800 t, 46%); no geotextile []
Confidence
medium

5 · Open issues

  • No true as-built plan-view CAD drawing or bathymetric survey was found publicly. The only plan-view figure available (design.jpg, legend 'ASR Design') is a pre-final concept sketch whose own two printed dimension arrows (110 m and 140 m) scale inconsistently by ~37% when pixel-measured — it was therefore used only for qualitative shape/taper topology, never for scaled vertex coordinates.
  • The design.jpg figure combines the physical reef outline with a separate wave-refraction/peel-line fan; distinguishing the two required close visual inspection and there remains some residual uncertainty about exactly where the rock structure's own edge lies versus the illustrative wave lines.
  • The two real aerial construction photos (, ) are both dated/captioned May 2025, i.e. mid-construction — they may show a partially-built extent rather than the completed footprint, so were used only to corroborate general taper direction, not final size.
  • Exact polygon vertices are a low-confidence synthetic estimate, constrained only by the sourced 165 m x 110 m bounding envelope and the qualitative crescent curvature described in the design table; treat the polygon as illustrative of shape family, not a precise outline.
  • area_m2 (9,720) is not a published figure — it is a geometric consequence of our assumed polygon and should be treated as low-confidence, same caveat as Gemini's own area figures.
  • The x-axis 'positive = north' convention is inferred from the apparent north-up orientation of the design figure (land west, water east, coast trending N-S) rather than from an explicit stated bearing or printed north arrow — flagged as an assumption.
  • Distance offshore has a documented range across sources (120 m per Wikipedia/, 140 m per the current page, ~145 m per a 2023 FAQ/) reflecting design evolution over time; we used the current page's 140 m figure as primary, consistent with the card.
  • Reef volume (34,000 m3) comes from an earlier 2017-bathymetry concept-stage table on the same figure as the shape sketch and may not equal the final as-built volume; only the final tonnage (62,800 t) is well corroborated across sources.
  • (City of Albany, May 2023 FAQ PDF), read in full during the 2026-09-25 verification pass, gives an earlier interim design of 'up to 100 metres in width' (vs the final 110 m) and an interim footprint of 'approximately 16,000m2' (vs our ~9,720 m2 estimate and Gemini's unsourced 13,500/12,363 m2) — consistent with the card's existing 'design evolution over time' framing for the offshore-distance figure, now shown to also apply to width and area. The current page's 165/110/140 figures were kept as primary, per existing methodology (prefer the final/current page over superseded interim estimates).
  • No individual designer name could be independently confirmed for this project as of the 2026-09-25 verification pass (see gemini_comparison.disagree, 'designer names'). Only the firm, Bluecoast Consulting Engineers, is confirmed (, 's consultant-team list); a prior draft's attribution of 'Evan Watterson' to this specific project did not hold up against its own cited sources and was withdrawn.

Elongated, rounded, asymmetric rock mound. Read off the two available plan-view graphics (the labelled aerial/schematic diagrams on Cru Collective's site, sourced from the project team) and cross-checked against the visible rock-shadow patch in the ABC News aerial photo, the mound tapers to a narrower, rounded point on its shoreward (near-shore) side and broadens to a blunter, rounded mass on its seaward (offshore) side — the opposite taper direction from Gemini's assumed 'apex seaward' chevron (see gemini_comparison). Long axis (160 m) treated as alongshore, short axis (80 m) as cross-shore, matching the conventional reading of '160 m long × 80 m wide' in every source, though no source explicitly labels which figure is alongshore vs cross-shore (flagged in open_issues). The reef sits in the lee of Palm Beach's natural offshore reef [], targeting dominant east-to-southeast swell [][], with sand naturally transported north along this stretch of coast [] — hence x-positive is defined as north. No source gives a numeric shoreline bearing or swell-approach angle; Gemini's '345° NNW shoreline / 090–110° swell' figures are not supported by any source we found and are not reproduced here.

5 · Open issues

  • Width (80 m vs Royal HaskoningDHV's own 144 m) and distance offshore (270 m vs Royal HaskoningDHV's own 330 m) remain unresolved across every source checked, including this one — carried forward unchanged from the card [].
  • No source explicitly states which published figure (160 m or 80 m) is the alongshore dimension vs the cross-shore dimension; we assumed 160 m = alongshore and 80 m = cross-shore, matching the conventional reading and Gemini's own assumption, but this is an inference, not a stated fact.
  • The point from which '270 m offshore' is measured (near edge, far edge, or centroid) is not specified by any source; we assumed centroid for simplicity, which shifts the true near/far edges by roughly ±40-45 m depending on which convention the original designers used.
  • Verification 2026-09-25 flags an internal tension: our own reading of the Cru Collective schematic (images_relied_on #1) concludes the '270m' arrow visually lands on the reef's near/shoreward edge, not its centroid — yet the polygon below places the centroid (not the near edge) at y=270. If the near-edge reading is right, the whole polygon should sit roughly 40m further offshore than drawn (shoreward tip near y=266 instead of y=226, centroid near y=310 instead of y=270). This was not corrected in the polygon itself (doing so would require a new speculative construction, which this adversarial-check task's scope does not extend to), but is flagged here as an unresolved self-consistency issue for a future revision.
  • No true as-built CAD drawing or bathymetric survey of the constructed reef was found publicly (despite Gemini's citation, which does not correspond to any real accessible document); our polygon's exact vertex geometry is a qualitative estimate from a non-scaled marketing schematic plus a real aerial photo, not a measurement, and should be treated as illustrative of shape family (elongated, rounded, shoreward-tapered mound) rather than a precise outline.
  • Precise lat/lon of the reef structure itself (as opposed to the 19th Avenue onshore reference point) was not found in any source.
  • Net footprint area (~9,678 m2 here) is a geometric consequence of our assumed polygon shape, not an independently published or measured figure; treat as low-confidence.

shoreline (approximate; the two sourced figures below are worded as "offshore"/"off the coast" without stating whether measured from MHW, MLW or the general shoreline)
Materials
Graded quarried rock armour, Type 1 (3–6 t), Type 3 (0.3–1 t), Type 4 (6–10 t) and Type 6 (5–100 kg), placed by land-based excavators via a temporary rock causeway; overall Phase 1 rock+shingle tonnage 275,000 t, of which roughly 77,200 t was graded rock armour (Types 1/3/4/6) shared across the reef, groynes and breakwaters together — not separable into a reef-only tonnage by any source found [] (reused from card)
Confidence
low overall for dimensions and crest depth; medium specifically for the higher-level fact that the structure is two separate/adjoining parts rather than one continuous berm (independent text corroboration: 's 'double reef', BAM Nuttall's 'northern and southern multi-purpose reef' captions); low/unconfirmed specifically for the finer claim of which part is oval-shaped vs hook-shaped and which is 'northern' vs 'southern' (this rests only on a generic, inconsistently-drawn map icon — see verification and orientation_notes)

4 · Gemini comparison (Gemini's values are unverified; shown only to explain differences)

Where we agree

  • General structure class (submerged rock reef/berm built from graded rock armour) matches our card and /.
  • Rough shoreline-parallel siting and a broadly SW/WSW-facing exposure are geographically plausible for a west-facing Cardigan Bay frontage, though the precise 230-260 degree figure is not confirmed by any source we could access (see orientation_notes).

Gemini's 200 m has no working citation behind it — none of its three listed sources ("Ceredigion County Council Final Review 2013", "BAM Nuttall Project Case Study 2012", "Coflein National Monuments Record 2015") could be located online this session (no URL was given for any of them, and none of the real, locatable documents from these same organisations that we found — the actual Coflein record, the actual New Civil Engineer article — contain a 200 m figure). Gemini's single continuous berm does not match any of this; its own internal audit document (scale_sketch_photo_alignment_audit.md) does not mention a two-part structure at all and marks the Borth entry "VERIFIED" with "no discrepancy", which this session's source-checking does not support.

We treat 1.2 m as plausible in general terms for a submerged multi-purpose reef of this kind, but unconfirmed and not something we can respectively verify or refute at the source, so we report it as an open gap rather than either agreeing or asserting a competing number.

5 · Open issues

  • VERIFICATION 2026-09-25 finding: the [] location diagram's 'Multi-Purpose Reef' legend icon (oval+hook) does not match the icon actually stamped at the reef's frontage location (a symmetric double-hook/bowtie shape), and that stamped icon is reused identically 6+ times elsewhere on the same diagram as a generic structure-location marker (including a second, previously undisclosed cluster within 'Completed Phase 1 Works' itself, not only in the Phase-2 span as the prior draft stated). It is unresolved this session whether that second Phase-1 cluster is a redundant second stamp of the same reef or a separate Phase-1 structure (e.g. a rock breakwater); this does not change the 'two separate parts' conclusion (independently text-sourced) but does mean the oval/hook sub-shapes and the north/south assignment in polygons_m should be read as an illustrative placeholder, not a schematic derived from a reliable figure.
  • VERIFICATION 2026-09-25 finding: max_dimension_m was recomputed from the raw polygons_m coordinates and corrected from 162 m (which was the bounding-box diagonal, sqrt(145^2+73^2), not an actual distance between any two polygon vertices) to 145.1 m (the true maximum pairwise vertex distance, achieved between a Lobe-A vertex near (-77,335) and a Lobe-B vertex near (68,330)), since the two lobes do not reach opposite corners of the bounding box.
  • Alongshore length, cross-shore width, footprint area and crest depth of the multi-purpose reef are NOT published in any source located or made accessible this session, including a newly-found primary design document (Royal HaskoningDHV/Ceredigion CC/Atkins public exhibition poster PDF, ). This mirrors the card's own 'gaps' list (reef crest depth/freeboard; reef footprint width and volume) and this session's research did not close those gaps, only narrowed the shape question.
  • The polygons_m in this file are an explicitly low-confidence, order-of-magnitude SCHEMATIC placeholder (method: analogy + rough tonnage scaling, not a measurement) — a future agent with access to the actual as-built survey, the ASR Ltd/HR Wallingford physical-model report, or a higher-resolution/CAD version of the Royal HaskoningDHV exhibition drawings would very likely be able to replace this with real numbers.
  • The New Civil Engineer article [] was blocked by WebFetch (HTTP 403) but was successfully fetched this session via a direct curl request with a browser-style User-Agent header; its full text was then read directly. This is worth noting for future agents who hit the same 403 with WebFetch on this domain.
  • The two-mound shape finding rests on one schematic location diagram [] whose icons are demonstrably reused elsewhere on the same page for generic Phase-2 structure locations; we are confident in the 'two adjoining mounds' topology (corroborated independently by 's 'double reef' wording and by the card's own BAM Nuttall photo captions) but not in the exact proportions/curvature drawn for each mound, nor in which mound is truly 'northern' vs 'southern' in the field.
  • Live satellite/aerial imagery (Bing Maps) inspected this session did not show a visually distinguishable offshore structure near the expected site; this is inconclusive (submerged rock reefs often do not show in calm, true-colour aerial imagery) and should not be read as evidence against the reef's existence or location.
  • Gemini's three cited sources for this reef ('Ceredigion County Council Final Review 2013', 'BAM Nuttall Project Case Study 2012', 'Coflein National Monuments Record 2015') could not be located anywhere online this session — no URL, no matching document title, and the two genuinely locatable organisations' own real pages (the actual Coflein record NPRN 424699, the actual New Civil Engineer article) do not contain Gemini's specific numbers. We treat all of Gemini's Borth-specific numeric claims as unverified at the source, per project rule, rather than adopting any of them.

3 · Coordinate conventions and notes

Coordinates
metres; origin = shoreline point (Tay St / Marine Parade waterline) nearest the reef centroid; x = alongshore (positive toward north, matching the sourced "northern arm" / "southern arm" naming in /Mead 2011 - exact compass bearing of this axis is not stated in any source, only the relative north/south naming of the two arms); y = offshore (positive seaward); shoreline approximated as the line y=0
Shape
chevron
Orientation
DESIGN intent (, NZ Geographic 2006, quoting designer Kerry Black): 'the apex of the V points seaward and the structure thickens towards the base' - i.e. a symmetric, seaward-pointing V/delta-wing widening toward the shore. AS-BUILT (per 's multibeam survey figures, Jan 2007 at 70% complete and July 2013): the realised structure is NOT a clean symmetric V - it is a bent, asymmetric two-arm shape (a 'northern arm' and a 'southern arm' meeting near a central apex/focus point, per 's own terminology, e.g. 'the focus structure at the apex'), with the northern arm's containers rendered as a roughly shore-parallel band and the southern arm's containers rendered as a roughly cross-shore band, meeting at an angle visually closer to ~90 degrees than to the narrow symmetric V shown in the ASR/raisedwaterresearch.com CAD rendering ('s 'Mount Reef' design image). This asymmetry is consistent with, and likely a direct consequence of, the well-documented staged/incomplete construction (western/northern side built and surfable from Nov 2005-Mar 2006; eastern/southern side still 'nearly to specifications' by Oct 2006; final completion not until mid-2008) and the ~47% volume shortfall. The polygon in this file models the AS-BUILT bent shape (two separate arm rectangles under polygons_m), not the idealised symmetric design V.
Area
Shoelace area of the polygon above: 2,497 m² (stored value 2,497 m²).
Crest depth datum
below Chart Datum (~ Lowest Astronomical Tide, LAT); DESIGN target was 0.4 m below LAT/Chart Datum; the most recent surveys (to 2013) found the MAJORITY of the as-built crest at 0.8-1.0 m below Chart Datum. s2.1 separately states that 'at its highest point, the reef is approximately 0.2 m below chart datum, or approximately 0.1 m below the lowest astronomical tide' -- this is ONE point expressed in two datums (not a 0.1-0.2 m range), and 's text does NOT say which arm it is on [CORRECTED 2026-09-25 verification pass: the original text here wrongly attributed this point to 'the northern arm crest', a detail invented by the prior pass and not present in 's own text]. s4.3.2.1 separately, and explicitly, states an isolated shallow spot on the SOUTHERN arm at 0.2-0.4 m below Chart Datum (July 2013 survey) -- given the similar depth and shared 'most recent survey' framing, this may be the same feature as the unattributed s2.1 point, but never states this equivalence, so both are kept as separate, uncombined source statements. The single 0.9 m value here is our own midpoint of the reported 0.8-1.0 m 'majority of the reef' figure, not itself a directly quoted number.
Distance measured from
shoreline (Tay St / Marine Parade waterline) Convergent across five independent-ish accounts: (NZ Herald 2023) states 250 m directly; (BoPRC consent-application text) gives 250-300 m; (NZ Geographic 2006, quoting designer Kerry Black) gives 250 m; (raisedwaterresearch.com) explains the reef was DESIGNED for 300 m but built ~50 m closer due to Port of Tauranga dredge-disposal-area constraints, i.e. ~250 m as sited; (NZ Herald, Nov 2005, pre-completion) gives 240 m. We treat 250 m as the best-supported as-sited figure and 300 m as the superseded original design target.
Materials
Sand-filled non-woven geotextile 'megacontainers' on a securing mesh/web lattice pulled to the seabed [][][][]. Design called for up to 24 large cylindrical bags [] (the largest 3.5 m high x 50 m long, holding 660 m3 each []; alternatively described elsewhere as bags 'up to 60 m long x 5 m diameter' [] - these two bag-size descriptions do not match each other and neither source reconciles the difference, see open_issues). As-built, (citing Mead 2011) instead describes 6 containers per arm (3 large crest containers + 3 smaller base containers per side, 12 total design, with the as-built base containers substituted for shorter units) - a third, different container-count description that also does not reconcile with 's '24 bags' figure.
Confidence
medium

4 · Gemini comparison (Gemini's values are unverified; shown only to explain differences)

Where we agree

  • Distance offshore (~250 m): matches our own best-supported figure exactly, and both are independently corroborated by multiple sources on our side (, , , 's derivation) - genuine agreement, not coincidence.
  • General shape family ('chevron' / V-with-two-arms): Gemini's 'chevron' classification and our own (also 'chevron', built from two named arms) agree at the topology level, even though the specific polygon coordinates and gross/net dimensions disagree substantially (see below).
  • Net footprint/arm area (~2,455 m2 Gemini vs our 2,497 m2): close numerical agreement, though reached by very different methods and starting bounding dimensions - we treat this as a loose corroboration at best, not confirmation, given how differently each figure was derived.
  • Design crest depth in the same ballpark: Gemini's own footprint-notes mention 'Designed for -0.5m LAT', close to our sourced 0.4 m below LAT design target [] - a genuine partial match on the DESIGN figure specifically.

shape topology ("inverted Y" vs bent two-arm chevron)"Swept-Wing Inverted Y / Chevron with Central Ridge" - implying three distinct members (a central ridge/stem plus two swept wings) and a broadly symmetric layout, per Gemini's own 10-vertex polygonTwo arms only (northern, southern per /Mead 2011's own naming), no separate central ridge/stem member, meeting at a single apex/focus point at a bend that visual inspection of 's own survey figures puts closer to ~90 degrees than to a narrow symmetric V or a three-limbed Y (an official report directly describing the physical structure from diver inspections and repeated multibeam surveys) consistently describes exactly TWO arms ("6 geotextile containers on each side", "the northern arm", "the southern arm") plus a single shared "apex" - never a third, separate "central ridge" component. 5 · Open issues

  • The polygons_m vertex coordinates are our own estimate: the overall bounding envelope (80x70 m / 67.8x72.9 m as modelled) is well-sourced [, cross-checked by ], but the specific bend angle (~90 degrees) and the arm-length split (55 m northern / 45 m southern) used to place individual vertices were read qualitatively off 's survey figures, not measured to a calibrated scale - we could not extract a reliable metres-per-pixel scale from the rendered PDF page images for Figure 3. Treat individual vertex positions as +/-15 m uncertain even though the overall envelope is high-confidence.
  • Three different, mutually inconsistent design-volume figures now exist across sources: ~5,000 m3 [], 6,000 m3 [, ], and 6,500 m3 [] - none of the sources reconciles this with the others; all describe the same 'design' stage, not different stages.
  • Two different, mutually inconsistent container/bag-size and bag-count descriptions exist: describes 24 bags total, the largest 3.5 m high x 50 m long holding 660 m3 each; describes bags 'up to 60 m long and 5 m in diameter'; (via Mead 2011) instead describes 6 containers per arm (12 total in the base design: 3 large crest + 3 smaller base containers per side). No source reconciles these three accounts, and it is unclear whether they describe the same design stage, different design revisions, or a reporting error.
  • Gemini's three cited sources ('Black, S.M. & Kerry, A. 1999' - already in our own reference list as /design-paper citation; 'Mead, S. et al. 2007 Mount Maunganui Reef Monitoring Report, ASR Ltd'; 'Tauranga City Council: Tay Street Reef Removal Dossier 2014') could not be independently located by us. The 1999 design paper is the same one our card already cites via Lior's notes [] and we did not find an accessible copy of it either (a design paper WITH plan-view figures and precise original design dimensions, if locatable, would likely be the single best remaining source to check against both our and Gemini's numbers - flagged for a possible future pass, not pursued further here as it is not yet in either project's accessible reference set).
  • Exact real-world compass bearing of the shoreline / the alongshore (x) axis at Mount Maunganui Beach is not stated in any source we accessed; we used the sourced 'northern arm' / 'southern arm' naming [] to fix positive-x = north, which is better-grounded than a fully arbitrary convention but still does not give an exact bearing in degrees.
  • The as-built shape shown in 's July 2013 survey (5 years after 2008 completion, after documented bag deflation/sand-leakage damage 'near the apex of the structure') may itself have degraded/settled somewhat from the as-completed-in-2008 geometry; we did not find an earlier, immediately-post-completion (2008) survey figure to check against, only the January 2007 (70%-complete) and July 2013 figures.
  • Crest_depth_m.value (0.9 m) is our own midpoint of a stated 0.8-1.0 m range, not itself a directly quoted single figure - see the derivation table row and the crest_depth_m field's own notes.
  • [ADDED 2026-09-25 verification pass] A direct pixel-level zoom into 's Figure 3 (July 2013 survey) shows a small, separate reddish-orange (shallow) blob near the apex/junction of the two arms, detached from both main limbs by a deeper (blue) gap. No source text names a distinct third feature here - /Mead 2011 consistently describe exactly two arms plus a shared apex - so this is recorded only as our own unsourced visual observation, of uncertain origin (possibly the repaired/replaced T4 bag documented near the apex, a small isolated remnant, or bathymetric noise), not as a basis for revising shape_type. It is noted here only because it is the one respect in which Gemini's 'with Central Ridge' framing is not obviously wrong, even though Gemini's own specific description (a swept-back three-limbed Y) does not match what is visible either.

3 · Coordinate conventions and notes

Coordinates
metres; origin = shoreline point nearest the reef centroid (approx. the beach access point at the southern end of Bargara Beach, near Bill Fritz Park / Burkitt Street, Bargara); x = alongshore (positive toward north, approximate -- Bargara's coastline trends roughly N-S here; no source gives an exact shoreline azimuth); y = offshore (positive seaward, approximately east into the Coral Sea); shoreline approximated as the line y=0. Because the reef is an attached headland (not a detached structure), much of its landward edge lies at or near y=0.
Shape
Not an engineered structure with a designed plan-view template -- Burkitts Reef is a natural basalt headland/rock shelf that was reshaped in place (existing boulders broken down and relocated with a rented excavator) rather than built from new imported material. None of V/delta/chevron/linear/crescent/L/mound describes a natural point/headland reef, so 'other' is used. The polygon below traces the visible natural rock/reef extent read off satellite imagery -- it is NOT a surveyed or designed footprint, and no such footprint has ever been published for this reef (confirmed against our own card, which already states 'No footprint length/width figure found', and against every source checked in this pass).
Orientation
Attached headland/point at the southern end of Bargara Beach (near Bill Fritz Park / Burkitt Street) trending roughly NNE-SSW, with its rocky tip projecting seaward (east) into the Coral Sea. Consistently described as a 'right-hand point break' (,): the wave wraps the point and peels back toward the beach, putting the wave face on the surfer's right as they ride it, which is only possible with the seaward apex/densest boulder mass lying to the north/east of the main takeoff zone. No source gives a precise compass bearing or arm angle -- this description is drawn from (a) the plan shape visible in satellite imagery (see images_relied_on) and (b) Greg Redgard's own 1980 hand-drawn petition sketch, which labels a dense boulder mass 'BURKITTS REEF' at the seaward/outer end of a wedge-shaped point, shows a cleared 'swimmers passage' / 'boat passage' channel along the shoreward side, and marks hazard rocks with 'X' roughly midway along the point -- consistent with the satellite-imagery shape and with the Esplanade/houses/Basin/golf-course landmarks also visible on today's satellite imagery.
Area
Shoelace area of the polygon above: 2,480 m² (stored value 2,480 m²).
Crest depth datum
exposed dry basalt at low tide (the condition under which the 1997 excavator work was done); rises to roughly 2.5 m of water depth over the same rock at high spring tide
Crest depth over time
This is not a single engineered crest depth -- Burkitts Reef is an intertidal rock platform whose water cover varies continuously with the tide. No source publishes a fixed crest elevation against a survey datum (e.g. LAT). The 0 m (dry) to ~2.5 m (submerged) range is our own inference from 's stated ~2.5 m local tide swing, not a direct measurement. Corrected 2026-09-25: an earlier draft of this file also cited for the ~2.5 m figure; (Swellnet, re-fetched) corroborates the 1982/1997 timeline and before/after surf-day counts but does not itself restate a tide-swing number, so it has been removed from this citation. Gemini's file gives the same order-of-magnitude range (0.2-2.5 m) but does not tie it to either of its own two relevant sources.
Distance measured from
shoreline
Materials
Natural volcanic basalt boulders (existing headland rock), reshaped in place -- not new material. ~300 m3 of rock relocated, at least 12 large boulders broken down/repositioned, gaps hand-packed with bricks; some old discarded railway-track iron was also present in the rock and cleared [][][][][] (all figures already in the verified card; not re-derived here).
Confidence
low

4 · Gemini comparison (Gemini's values are unverified; shown only to explain differences)

Where we agree

  • distance_offshore_m -- Gemini is right that this is not an offshore structure; we make this explicit as a sourced value of 0 m rather than leaving it blank.
  • General direction of the crest_depth_m claim (an intertidal platform that is dry at low tide and covered at high tide) -- we independently derive the same order-of-magnitude range from 's stated ~2.5 m tide swing, though not from any of Gemini's own 4 listed sources.
  • Gemini's own 'suspicious' flag that its 80m x 40m figure has zero citation pinning it to any of its 4 listed references -- we confirm this independently (see disagree below) and go further: one of the 4 references appears to be a dead/fabricated link.
QuantityGeminiOursWhy ours
length_m / width_m80 x 40 (uncited prose, no source pins it)~120 x ~46 (satellite-imagery scale-bar estimate, source )We checked all 4 of Gemini's cited sources for this reef. (1) Gemini's ABC News URL (.../2024-01-21/burkitts-reef-bundaberg-greg-redgard-surfing/103328224) returns HTTP 404 -- it does not exist. The real ABC News article we cite (, dated 2024-01-28, a different URL/slug) was re-checked directly and contains no dimensions at all. (2)-(4) 'The Inertia', 'Swellnet Australia' and 'Tracks Magazine' in Gemini's reference list are bare homepage links (theinertia.com, swellnet.com, tracksmag.com.au) with no article-specific URL, so '80m x 40m' cannot be traced to any of them. We instead measured the visible natural rock/reef point on Google Maps satellite imagery using its on-screen scale bar and got a larger, differently-proportioned footprint. Both figures are estimates rather than published measurements, but ours is tied to a specific, checkable method and source; Gemini's is not.
shape_typeN/A -- no CAD entry / not drawnother (a rough polygon is now drawn from satellite imagery, clearly flagged as an estimate)Gemini is correct that no engineered CAD footprint exists for this reef -- we agree with that core point. But a rough natural-extent polygon can still be produced from a real, citable image with a stated method and uncertainty, which we provide here for the first time rather than leaving the field entirely blank.
crest_depth_m0.2 to 2.5 (prose, no source pinned to either of the 2 sources that might plausibly cover it)0 (exposed) to ~2.5 (submerged at high spring tide) -- same order of magnitude, re-derived directly from 's stated ~2.5 m tide swingGemini's number is directionally reasonable but, like the 80x40 figure, is not tied to any of its own 4 cited sources. We derive the same range from 's explicitly stated tide-swing figure, which is already in our verified card, and frame it as an inferred intertidal range rather than a measured crest depth.

5 · Open issues

  • Burkitts Reef is a natural basalt headland reshaped in place, not an engineered structure -- no source (ours or Gemini's) publishes a plan-view footprint, so every geometric figure in this file (polygon, length, width, area) is our own visual estimate from satellite imagery, not a surveyed or designed footprint. Treat with low confidence.
  • The boundary of 'the reef' versus the surrounding sandy/rocky shore is inherently fuzzy and was judged by eye from satellite imagery; a different analyst could reasonably draw a materially different polygon of a different size.
  • Precise reef coordinates are not published (already flagged in our verified card); the lat/lon on the card is Bargara town centre, not the reef itself. The polygon here is in local metres relative to an approximate shoreline origin, not tied to a surveyed lat/lon.
  • No source gives a compass bearing or numeric arm angle for the point; orientation is qualitative only.
  • Gemini's ABC News reference for this reef (URL ending 103328224, dated 2024-01-21) returned HTTP 404 during verification -- it appears to be a dead or fabricated link, a distinct problem from (and in addition to) the uncited '80m x 40m' figure already flagged in the task brief.
  • Visualization / adding this reef to a comparison-scale UI tab in 04_build is outside the scope of this footprint-research task; this file only produces the researched JSON and provenance doc.

3 · Coordinate conventions and notes

Coordinates
metres; origin = shoreline point nearest the reef centroid; x = alongshore (positive toward north, per 's 'from north to south' length description — no source states which specific end/arm is the northern one, treated as a stated but not surveyed convention); y = offshore (positive seaward); shoreline approximated as the line y=0
Shape
V
Orientation
Plan shape is a 'V'/chevron ('boomerang') mound with two unequal arms (left-hand ride 30-40 m, right-hand ride 50-80 m per ) meeting at a single apex. Whether the apex points offshore (toward the incident swell) or onshore (toward the beach) could not be conclusively read from the only available plan-view figures ( Figures 4 and 7, low-resolution 1999 photocopies with illegible scale bars). This file assumes apex-offshore (the standard configuration for point-break-style chevron surf reefs, and consistent with 's text describing the fill as 'extending the existing 3 m depth contour offshore' while the arms merge with the natural reef inshore) - flagged low confidence. The reef's overall alongshore axis runs north-south per ; no source gives which arm is north. Design-era swell assumption (): 'predominantly from the west' - no specific compass bearing for the final built structure's orientation was found in any source (Gemini's precise '240-270 deg WSW' figure is unverified/unsourced).
Area
Shoelace area of the polygon above: 2,299 m² (stored value 2,299 m²).
Crest depth datum
below the water surface on average tides (as-built design range 1-3 m per ; 1.5 m point estimate is the card's already-cited ~2009-review figure, below the lowest tide)
Distance measured from
shoreline (approximate; does not specify MSL vs low-tide reference line)
Materials
Granite boulders, more than 10,000 tons, individual boulders up to 3 m across, placed on the existing natural limestone reef/bedrock [][][]; two other sources (card's /) instead describe the placed rock as limestone - unresolved disagreement, carried from the verified card. Volume of rock: 3,500 m3 (Wikipedia, ) vs ~5,000 m3 (ICM, ) - also unresolved.
Confidence
medium

  • The 250 m (, pre-final-design) vs 275 m (, final) offshore-distance figures may reflect the card's already-documented mid-construction southern-end extension, but no source explicitly connects the two numbers - an inference, not a confirmed explanation.

3 · Coordinate conventions and notes

Coordinates
metres; origin = shoreline point nearest the reef centroid (approximated at the base of the rocky headland/‘Lighthouse Point’ immediately updrift of the reef); x = alongshore, positive toward the southeast (from the headland toward the main Lighthouse Beach hotel frontage, matching the sense of ASR Ltd's own construction-phase aerial photo, ) — the true compass bearing of this alongshore direction was not found in any source and this sense is inferred from photo geometry only; y = offshore, positive seaward; shoreline approximated as the line y=0
Shape
As-built structure appears to be an echelon/fan array of individual ~30 m geotextile bag units radiating from a focus near the rocky headland, producing a stepped/zigzag breaking line — NOT a single smooth curved crescent or delta wedge. Based on two independent photographic sources (/ ASR Ltd's own construction-phase aerial photo, and Raised Water Research's traced wave-break outline). Medium confidence on typology; the exact number/angles of units is a schematic reconstruction (low confidence).
Polygon
SCHEMATIC RECONSTRUCTION, not an as-built survey polygon — no engineering drawing or GPS as-built survey of the Kovalam reef was found in any source (ours or Gemini's). Constructed as three ~30 m geotextile-tube units (matching the sourced '30 m units' fact, //) chained in a staggered/echelon 'staircase' with a 12 m tube width (width itself not sourced for Kovalam; borrowed by analogy from comparable ASR Ltd geobag reef crest widths, e.g. Gold Coast/Mt Maunganui-family designs, and from Gemini's own unsourced 12 m crest-width assumption, which is plausible but likewise unverified). Verified closed and non-self-intersecting with shapely (is_valid=True, is_simple=True, first vertex == last vertex).
Orientation
The unit fan appears to originate from a focus close to the rocky headland ('Eve's/Lighthouse Point' area) immediately updrift of Lighthouse Beach, with the geotextile-tube units fanning alongshore toward the main hotel-fronted beach and outward to sea (per 's aerial photo, where a labelled 'Reef' shows several dark parallel/sub-parallel submerged tube-rows radiating from near the point). No compass bearing for the arms, the shoreline, or the incident swell was found specifically sourced for Kovalam; Gemini's swell-direction figure (200–240° SSW) is a generically plausible Arabian Sea SW-monsoon swell window but is not independently confirmed for this exact site in any source read this pass.
Area
This is the footprint of the geobag tubes themselves (slender fan, ~12 m wide), not a filled solid wedge — substantially smaller than Gemini's candidate (3,800 m² gross / 2,245 m² by their own polygon-area audit) because we model the structure as an open fan of narrow tubes, consistent with the photographic evidence in , rather than a solid crescent/delta mass. Low confidence — order-of-magnitude estimate only.
Crest depth datum
not found No source (ours, Gemini's cited sources, or this pass's independent search) states a crest/submergence depth for the as-built Kovalam reef. Gemini's 1.6 m value traces to two citations ('Kerala Harbour Engineering Dept Project Report 2011' and 'Thomas et al. 2012 Performance Assessment of Kovalam Multipurpose Reef') that could not be located or confirmed to exist under those titles/years in this pass's search (see gemini_comparison). By loose analogy, comparable ASR Ltd geotextile multi-purpose reefs (Mount Maunganui, Narrowneck) sit roughly 1.5–2.5 m below chart datum, but this is a generic analogy, not a Kovalam-specific figure, and is not asserted as fact.
Distance measured from
shoreline (schematic y=0 baseline) Not published in any source. Our schematic polygon's inner edge sits ~34 m and outer edge ~76 m from the shoreline baseline (centroid ~55 m); this range is a low-confidence visual impression from the ASR Ltd construction-phase aerial photo (), where swimmers/snorkellers are shown very close to both the shore and the reef, suggesting a near-shore siting broadly compatible with, but not confirming, Gemini's specific 150 m figure. Gemini's 150 m could not be verified against any accessible source either.
Materials
Non-woven geotextile sand-filled containers ('Geotubes'/bags), built in ~30 m-long units [][]. (Geosynthetics Magazine) discusses Kovalam only as an example of geotextile-bag failure ("debris strikes (Kovalam)") and does not itself state the 30 m unit length -- removed from this citation on re-verification (2026-09-25).
Confidence
low

Where we agree

  • A generically SW-monsoon-driven swell climate at this coast is directionally plausible (not Kovalam-specific verified, but consistent with regional knowledge).

5 · Open issues

  • No engineering drawing, GPS as-built survey, or dimensioned figure for the Kovalam reef was found in this pass (ours or Gemini's) — all footprint numbers here (ours and Gemini's) are estimates of varying rigor, not sourced as-built dimensions.
  • Gemini's two cited sources for crest depth/dimensions ('Kerala Harbour Engineering Dept Project Report 2011', 'Thomas et al. 2012') could not be located; they may be fabricated, badly mis-cited, or simply inaccessible online — flagged, not resolved.
  • Mead, S.T. and Borrero, J.C. (2011) 'Multi-Purpose Reefs – A Decade of Application' is very likely the actual technical source behind Raised Water Research's uncredited 'Mead and Borrero (2011)' reference and may contain real Kovalam performance/dimension data, but it sits behind ResearchGate/eCoast gates (eCoast requires an email-gated download) and could not be read this pass.
  • The 12 m tube/crest-width assumption used in our area estimate is not sourced for Kovalam specifically — borrowed by analogy from other ASR Ltd geobag reefs and from Gemini's own (also unsourced) assumption.
  • The compass bearing of the shoreline/alongshore direction and of the incident swell was not confirmed for this exact site in any source read this pass.
  • The 'Kovalam-Outline.jpg' hand-traced line could represent either the structure's crest outline or simply the visible foam/break-line pattern at one moment of one swell — sources do not label which, so its use here as shape evidence carries residual uncertainty.
  • Re-verification pass (2026-09-25) also opened three more images already hosted on the already-cited page but not previously catalogued -- Kovalam-Geomat.jpg (a construction-beach photo of a large woven/mesh fabric sheet being hauled ashore with orange floats, headland visible offshore) and Kovalam-Reef-Underwater1.jpg / -Underwater2.jpg (close-range underwater shots of a smooth rounded mound with small fish, no scale reference) -- plus Gemini's own three cited photos (kovalam-reef-india.jpg, _gallery1.jpg, _gallery2.jpg). None of these six images contributed any new dimension or changed any number: the Geomat photo's exact role (base filter mat vs. the bag fabric itself) is not captioned or explained anywhere and is left unresolved; the underwater shots corroborate a smooth single-mound/tube-like structure at close range but carry no scale bar; Gemini's own three cited photos show no reef outline at all (see gemini_comparison, new finding).

3 · Coordinate conventions and notes

Coordinates
metres; origin = shoreline point nearest the reef centroid; x = alongshore (positive toward the cove headland side referred to in sources as the reef's flank, true compass direction not published — treated as arbitrary +x); y = offshore (positive seaward); shoreline approximated as the line y=0
Shape
other (single-arm wedge, schematic)
Orientation
No plan-view figure, survey drawing or compass bearing for the Opunake reef was found in any accessible source (- in the card, nor Gemini's cited-but-inaccessible 'Mead & Black 2007 Design Dossier' / 'Taranaki Regional Council Monitoring Records 2010'). The polygon here is a SCHEMATIC placeholder only: a symmetric isosceles wedge with its 20 m base at the shoreward (inshore) end and its apex pointing offshore (seaward), by direct analogy to the one Opunake-designer reef whose plan geometry IS described in a primary source in our reference list — Mount Maunganui, built by the same firm (ASR Ltd) around the same time, explicitly described as having its 'apex... point[ing] seaward and the structure thicken[ing] towards the base' []. Opunake's own sources (, ) state only that the reef's bags 'cover an area around 90m long and 20m wide' with no shape description; / also both note the design was for a single 'right-hand wave' (one peel direction), unlike Mount Maunganui's two-directional wave off a symmetric V — meaning the real Opunake reef almost certainly had an ASYMMETRIC wedge/arm (like the 'asymmetric polygonal wedge' shape of the comparable Cables Reef), not the symmetric triangle drawn here. We chose the symmetric schematic deliberately rather than inventing a specific asymmetric skew, because no source gives which flank was the long peeling shoulder or the arm's angle to the shoreline. Distance offshore and crest depth are both low-confidence estimates (see derivation) since neither figure is published for Opunake specifically in any source we could access.
Area
Shoelace area of the polygon above: 900 m² (stored value 900 m²).
Crest depth datum
unknown — no datum stated in any accessible source; treat as approximate depth below mean sea level
Distance measured from
shoreline (estimated centroid distance, not a surveyed figure)
Materials
27 sand-filled geotextile ('geo-container') bags [][] (card). CORRECTED 2026-09-25: the fabric spec 'non-woven, polyester/polyester-polypropylene' previously cited to [][] does not appear in either source's text (re-fetched in full); that exact material description is 's account of Mount Maunganui's bags, not Opunake's, and was misattributed. Opunake's own bag fabric composition is not published in any source we could access.
Confidence
medium

4 · Gemini comparison (Gemini's values are unverified; shown only to explain differences)

Where we agree

  • Overall verdict/status framing ('partially built / underperforming', single arm only built) matches our card's independently-sourced account [][][].
  • 150 m distance offshore: we ended up at the same number, but reached it independently by a completely different (and equally unconfirmed) method — see derivation. Treat the match as coincidental corroboration at best, not confirmation.
  • ~1.4-1.5 m crest depth: our independent rough estimate (1.5 m, +-1.0 m) overlaps Gemini's figure, but neither is a sourced fact.

5 · Open issues

  • No primary source with an actual plan-view drawing, survey, or CAD figure for the Opunake reef was found or was accessible (NZ Geographic 's full text has no figures/images at all and does not contain the 90x20 figure; ResearchGate is blocked by Cloudflare on both WebFetch and curl, exactly as already flagged in the card).
  • The card's citation of the 90x20 footprint as [][][] is only fully supported by and ; 's accessible text does not contain this figure. Worth a small correction pass on the card/dossier (not made here, per the task's Gemini-folder read-only / no-new-facts-into-card-without-a-separate-pass convention) — flagging it here as an open issue instead.
  • Crest depth and distance offshore are not published anywhere we could find for Opunake specifically; both values here are low-confidence estimates, clearly separable in the JSON from the two solidly-sourced dimensions (90 m / 20 m).
  • The true left/right asymmetry of the reef (it produced only a right-hand wave, unlike the symmetric two-directional Mount Maunganui V) is not captured by the symmetric schematic polygon used here, because no source specifies the arm's actual skew or compass angle.
  • Gemini's two cited sources for its dimensions ('Mead & Black 2007 Design Dossier', 'Taranaki Regional Council Environmental Monitoring Records 2010') could not be located or accessed by us at all -- not on ResearchGate, not via a direct fetch, not anywhere in either project's folders -- so Gemini's numbers could not be confirmed at the source and are not adopted, per project rule.

3 · Coordinate conventions and notes

Coordinates
metres; origin = shoreline point nearest the reef centroid; x = alongshore (positive toward the arm drawn 'up' in the Skelly Engineering plan-view drawing - no source gives a compass bearing or north arrow, so this is an arbitrary, stated-but-unverified convention, same limitation as the parallel cables-reef-wa.md file); y = offshore (positive seaward); shoreline approximated as the line y=0
Shape
V (asymmetric chevron)
Orientation
The reinforced central 'spine' block (where the two arms of bags converge) is the most-offshore point of the structure and faces the 'WAVE DIRECTION' arrow drawn on the Skelly Engineering plan view, i.e. the apex points seaward into the incident swell, consistent with the card's design narrative ('arms at roughly 45 degrees to the predominant swell, meant to focus and peel incoming waves'). The drawing's own 45-degree angle annotation (measured from a vertical reference line to one arm) and this file's pixel-geometry check (~92 degrees between the two arms, i.e. ~46 degrees each side of the wave-direction axis) agree closely. The two arms are markedly ASYMMETRIC: ~44 m from spine to one tip, ~33 m to the other (a ~25% difference) - a refinement on Gemini's near-symmetric 9-vertex polygon. No compass bearing for the wave-direction axis, and no indication of which arm points which alongshore (e.g. north vs south) direction, could be determined from the design drawing itself (no north arrow). Gemini's specific '260-280 deg, W-WNW' bearing is plausible for a Santa Monica Bay/El Segundo south-/west-facing beach but is not confirmed in any source in our card or found in this pass.
Plan box note
raw drawing measurement recomputed to ~57 m in the 2026-09-25 verification pass (see derivation table); polygon bbox (57.8 m) unchanged
Area
Shoelace area of the polygon above: 324 m² (stored value 324 m²).
Crest depth datum
below MSL (design minimum, per the original Skelly Engineering plan-view drawing's own annotation 'TOP OF BAG MIN DEPTH -6' MSL' at both arm tips; 6 ft = 1.83 m). Card's other cited sources give two additional, conflicting as-surveyed/as-reported figures on different datums: -0.9 m MLLW () and ~2.4 m/8 ft at zero tide (, Surfrider-sourced, quoted by a Surfline commenter) - not resolved here, likely partly a datum (MSL vs MLLW vs 'zero tide') difference.
Distance measured from
shoreline (approximate; card's states only '~100 yards/100 m off the beach', not a precise engineering survey; ~100 yards = 91.4 m)
Materials
~200 sand-filled geotextile (described as polyester/black polypropylene) bags total, built in two phases: 110 bags fall 2000 (this drawing's exact bag count) + ~90 more bags spring 2001; individual bags ~14 tons () or ~14,000 lb () - sources disagree ~2x; bag footprint 3 m x 1.2 m per the Raised Water Research bag-size diagram () [][][][].

medium

4 · Gemini comparison (Gemini's values are unverified; shown only to explain differences)

Where we agree

  • Shape typology (V/chevron geobag array) is qualitatively correct - confirmed directly by the primary Skelly Engineering design drawing (), though our reading is a measurably ASYMMETRIC V (~44 m and ~33 m arms) rather than Gemini's implied near-symmetric 9-vertex polygon.
  • Crest depth (1.8 m) is very close to the '-6 ft MSL' (1.83 m) design-minimum-depth label we found directly on the original Skelly drawing () - though Gemini did not cite that drawing (it cites Henriquez/Surfrider/Borrero-Nelsen instead, none of which we could confirm state this figure), this specific number checks out against a primary source we located.
  • Distance offshore (95 m) falls within our own card's approximate '~100 yards/100 m' range () - reasonable agreement.

5 · Open issues

  • This file's Skelly-drawing-based measurements () describe the Phase I design only (110 bags + up to 30 'optional' bags = up to 140), matching the fall-2000 as-built count exactly. No plan-view drawing was found anywhere in our references for the spring-2001 Phase II addition (~90 more bags, bringing the total to ~200 built) - the FINAL as-built footprint (2001-2008) may have been somewhat larger than reported here, by an unknown amount.
  • The arm cross-section width (4 m) and spine-block size (8x6 m) used to turn the drawing's bag-chain centrelines into a closed polygon are this file's own estimate (from the bag-size diagram and visual inspection), not a published figure - area_m2 (324.1) should be read as order-of-magnitude only, not a precise footprint.
  • No compass bearing or north arrow appears on the Skelly drawing; this file's alongshore (x) axis direction is an arbitrary, stated-but-unverified convention (same limitation flagged in the parallel cables-reef-wa.md file for that reef).
  • The card's own two pre-existing crest-depth figures (-0.9 m MLLW per 's text vs ~2.4 m/8 ft at zero tide per ) remain unresolved; this file's new '-6 ft MSL' (1.83 m) reading from the drawing itself is a third data point, close to but not identical to either, plausibly a datum (MSL vs MLLW vs 'zero tide') difference rather than a genuine conflict - not resolved here.
  • image26.png's single '200 m' scale bar was shown (via the Narrowneck cross-check) not to transfer reliably across the graphic's 4 photo panels; its Pratte's-specific reading (~68.5x34.3 m) is reported for completeness in the derivation table only and is excluded from this file's headline/confidence-bearing numbers.
  • All pixel measurements come from a low-resolution (308x385 px) scanned engineering drawing; scale-bar tick-mark reading, bag-corner anti-aliasing, and line thickness contribute an estimated +/-10% uncertainty to every length/width/area figure derived from it.

3 · Coordinate conventions and notes

Coordinates
metres; origin = shoreline point nearest the reef centroid; x = alongshore (positive toward north, approximate -- Back Beach's coastline trends roughly N-S; no source gives an exact shoreline azimuth); y = offshore (positive seaward); shoreline approximated as the line y=0. Orientation is moot for a circle.
Shape
Not a V/delta/chevron/linear/crescent/L shape -- a single circular inflatable dome ('mound') with no arms or directional geometry.
Orientation
None -- the reef is a radially symmetric circular dome (12 m diameter in all directions), so it has no arms, apex, or preferred alongshore/offshore axis.
Area
Shoelace area of the polygon above: 112 m² (stored value 113 m²).
Crest depth datum
below the water surface at low tide (LAT, approximate)
Crest depth over time
Structure height above seabed is reported as 2 m in most contemporaneous sources (,,,) but as 1.6 m in one 2022 retrospective (); the 1.0 m crest-depth figure is a directly stated quote independent of which height figure is used.
Distance measured from
shoreline (design target range 30-45 m; 37.5 m is the midpoint)
Materials
Dome-shaped inflatable rubber (Hypalon, 5 mm thick) bladder with glued (not welded) seams; anchored to the seabed by partially filling it with sand, the rest of the bladder filled with water and air (: "The bladder is anchored to the seabed by partially filling it with sand. The rest of the bladder is filled with water and air."); total sand fill 140 tonnes (). Corrected 2026-09-25: an earlier draft quoted this as "washed, coarse beach sand" and omitted the water component -- that exact phrase does not appear on the page and has been replaced with the verbatim quote.

5 · Open issues

  • The reef was never completed (installation reached ~90% before a glued seam tore and the bladder was removed within days); every figure here is an as-designed value, not an as-installed/as-surveyed one.
  • Height above seabed is inconsistently reported: 2 m (,, contemporaneous) vs 1.6 m (1 later retrospective, ); 's imperial 'about 7-feet' is an approximate corroboration only, not an independent precise measurement.
  • and in the verified card cite the same raisedwaterresearch.com URL under two different reference ids -- likely a minor duplication in the card, noted here but not corrected (out of scope for this footprint-only task).
  • No exact installed lat/lon or surveyed offshore distance exists; 30-45 m is the pre-installation design target, sourced to only ( does not mention offshore distance).
  • Volume (117.3 m3) is our own geometric estimate, not a published figure; offered only as a sand-tonnage plausibility check.
  • Gemini's two cited sources for this reef ('Bottegal 2019 Project Brief', 'Surfer Magazine Trial Review 2020') could not be located or verified; treat Gemini's crest-depth and offshore-distance figures as unverified. Traced the specific mechanism of Gemini's 1.8 m crest-depth figure: it equals Gemini's own (unsourced) 3.8 m 'ambient seabed depth' input minus the 2.0 m height -- an internally consistent but externally unsupported calculation.
  • Attribution note: the earlier draft of this file's claim that Bunbury 'matches the flag already in Gemini's own suspicious notes' was imprecisely worded -- that 'suspicious' annotation ('one of the better-matched reefs') actually lives in OUR project's own intermediate extract file (07_scale/00_gemini_footprints_extract.json), not inside the Gemini folder itself. Gemini's own self-audit file (scale_sketch_photo_alignment_audit.md, row 11) independently marks Bunbury 'VERIFIED' with no discrepancy flagged. Both statements are substantively accurate; only the attribution of which file the note lives in has been corrected here.
  • Three citation errors found and fixed during 2026-09-25 adversarial verification: (1) (ABC 2019-06-13) was wrongly cited alongside for the 12 m diameter and the 30-45 m offshore distance -- re-fetched twice with targeted prompts and confirmed states ONLY the 2 m height, nothing else; (2) 's diameter quote was wrongly given the '(40 feet)' parenthetical that actually belongs to -- 's real text is metric-only ('two-metre-high, 12-metre-wide'); (3) (The Inertia) was quoted as giving a precise '6.5 feet' height when the actual (Wayback-Machine-verified, since the live URL 403s) text says 'about 7-feet high' -- a looser rounding. None of these fixes changed any headline number (12 m, 2 m, 1.0 m, 30-45 m all still hold on corrected citations), but the reference attributions have been corrected throughout. A fourth fix: the fill-material quote 'washed, coarse beach sand' was not actually found on the page and has been replaced with the verbatim quote (sand + water + air).

Method. Research agents gathered each reef's record from primary and secondary sources; separate agents then verified every claim against its cited source, and every image and video was checked to show the named site. Verification reports are kept in the project folder 05_qa. Only facts carrying a reference tag [R#] are shown; conflicts between sources are stated, not resolved. Dollar conversions marked approximate are rough, mostly unsourced estimates.

Some reviews and references were first spotted in a parallel survey made with another AI (Gemini). None was taken on trust: each was re-fetched from its original source and checked by our own agents before being added, and is tagged via Gemini survey, verified 2026-09-25.
